title: onprem/airgap: vendor offline bundle updates + add RKE2 CentOS/Alma/Rocky support and rollback tooling
author: Aisha Khan
commits: feat: vendor rke2-centos/almalinux/rocky images into offline bundle
chore: bump tuf metadata and include signed root/targets for offline updates
feat: add airgap-rollback tool (atomic rollback via bundle snapshot)
fix: helm values defaults for rke2 kubelet cgroup driver on CentOS-family
docs: upgrade notes + testing checklist for offline upgrades
description:
Background / motivation:
We continue to see customer demand for stronger distro coverage for on-prem air-gapped installs. Several Enterprise customers requested explicit support for CentOS-family nodes (CentOS 7/8 EOL users migrating to AlmaLinux/Rocky) when running RKE2 bundles. In addition, customers want safer offline upgrade paths with the ability to quickly roll back to a known-good bundle snapshot if there are regressions during an offline upgrade.

This PR: single continuous description string with checklist and details.
- Vendors CentOS/AlmaLinux/Rocky-compatible RKE2 images and package artifacts into the official offline bundle (installer/offline-bundles/rke2/*). Images are mirrored and re-tagged in our vendor registry with accompanying SBOM entries.
- Adds signed TUF metadata (root, targets) into installer/vendor/tuf to support verified offline updates and prevent accidental image substitution. We bumped targets metadata and included new image targets for the new distro artifacts.
- Introduces installer/scripts/airgap-rollback: a small POSIX-compatible helper that snapshots current cluster bundle manifests, applies upgrade bundles atomically, and can revert to the previous snapshot on failure. The script is intentionally small, documented, and guarded with dry-run mode.
- Helm chart changes: values-rke2-centos.yaml provides distro-specific kubelet/cgroup and sysctl defaults, a new nodeSelector/taint example for RKE2 on CentOS-family nodes, and clearer tolerations for SELinux/perf tweaks.
- Terraform: minor variable/shim fixes for the onprem module so the offline bundle path and checksum are plumbed correctly (fixes a bug where bundle path was optional and caused provisioning to skip airgap extraction).
- Tests and docs: adds a smoke e2e script for internal canary and updates docs/onprem/airgap-upgrades.md with upgrade/rollback instructions and known caveats.

Testing performed:
- Local bundle build and validation using the bundle-ci pipeline (CI initially failed on helm lint; fixed values and re-ran).
- TUF metadata verification step added to the bundle pipeline; verified offline install succeeds with metadata present.
- End-to-end smoke run against a small RKE2 cluster using AlmaLinux 8.9 nodes in our internal lab (installer/tests/e2e/airgap/rke2-centos-smoke.sh).
- Manual rollback exercises: tested airgap-rollback with induced upgrade failure; verified cluster rolled back to previous manifests and services recovered.

Migration notes / operator guidance:
- Operators must regenerate their airgap bundle and replace the existing offline bundle if they want CentOS/Alma/Rocky images included. The TUF root/targets files are part of the bundle; ensure your distribution process preserves signatures.
- For clusters using our terraform onprem module, set the new variable `offline_bundle_path` to point to the vendor bundle and provide `offline_bundle_checksum` (SHA256) to secure the pipeline.
- Rolling upgrades: recommended to run airgap-rollback --dry-run first, then a canary node upgrade before mass upgrades. Docs include a step-by-step.

Checklist:
- [x] Vendor images & update images-list.txt
- [x] Add TUF metadata and update bundle manifest
- [x] Implement airgap-rollback with dry-run and snapshot mode
- [x] Helm values + chart validation
- [x] Terraform variable fix and basic unit test
- [x] E2E smoke test and doc updates

Related linear/Jira: ENG-4312 (airgap distro support), ENG-4380 (rollback tooling), SUP-9023 (customer support case).

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids automatic cluster-side changes; the rollback tool is opt-in and requires operator invocation. We preserved backwards compatibility for existing bundles (no breaking changes to manifest schema).
